title: Strategic choices: Pick between two good options and accept the painful consequences
summary: Real strategy is a small set of macro-level choices between two genuinely good options, with all consequences accepted. Platitudes like "great design" are non-decisions. Good choices have real alternatives, explicit downsides, and reinforce each other so decentralized teams compound instead of dilute.

principles.text: Autonomous teams still need alignment on a few macro-level strategic choices, not tactics or platitudes.
principles.quote: Not alignment on tactics (those change weekly), nor on platitudes (those change nothing), but alignment on a small set of macro-level decisions. These are the **strategic choices**.

principles.text: A strategy that never says no is not a strategy; saying no even to universally desirable things is the hallmark.
principles.quote: A strategy that never says "no" is not a strategy. It should say "no" most of the time; that's a signal that you are actually [focusing]

principles.text: A real choice has a smart opposite: many successful companies have chosen each side. If the opposite is nonsense, it's a platitude.
principles.quote: "Good design" isn't a real choice because "bad design" was never a smart alternative.

principles.text: Every strategic choice is a package deal. Write the unfortunate consequences into the strategy so the whole company can apply it.
principles.quote: A strategic choice is a package deal: you don't get advantages without weaknesses.

principles.text: Aim for mutually reinforcing choices, not merely consistent ones. Check second-order effects for hidden conflicts, then interlock them.
principles.quote: Even better than "not conflicting" is "reinforcing." "Extensible" helps the product be "feature-rich." A small team forces the core to stay small, maintaining space for the ecosystem to thrive.

principles.text: When the choice conflicts, follow it; when it doesn't, take the best of both. Never settle for a balance that satisfies no one.
principles.quote: When in conflict, adhere to the strategic choice. When not in conflict, do whatever is best.
